title: The IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice (CMA P2-F · feeds REG/AUD)
lessonHtml:
Cold open — the $47,200.00 gap you are not allowed to round away

Real MBG fact: the 102.1 bank-reconciliation gap is proven at exactly $47,200.00, and Account 111 must clear to exactly $0.00. Ethics for a management accountant is not abstract — it is the discipline that forbids summarizing that gap away, reporting an approximate balance, or presenting a number the bank does not support. The IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice is the profession's code, and CMA Part 2 closes on it because every technique in the prior eleven months depends on the integrity of the numbers feeding it.

The four overarching standards

The IMA Statement sets four standards every member must uphold:

  • Competence — maintain professional expertise, perform duties per relevant laws and technical standards, provide accurate and timely decision support, and recognize and communicate professional limitations.
  • Confidentiality — keep information confidential except when disclosure is authorized or legally required, do not use confidential information for personal advantage, and ensure subordinates protect it.
  • Integrity — mitigate actual conflicts of interest and avoid apparent conflicts, refrain from conduct that would prejudice carrying out duties ethically, and abstain from activity that discredits the profession.
  • Credibility — communicate information fairly and objectively, disclose all relevant information that could influence a user's understanding, and disclose delays or deficiencies in information, timeliness, processing, or internal controls.

Mapping the standards to MBG's work

Credibility is why the $47,200.00 gap and the exact $95,000.00 in Account 111 are reported to the penny and disclosed, not smoothed. Integrity is why an accountant does not accept a certificate of insurance naming the wrong insured or quietly approve a payment they have a personal interest in. Competence is why JCS exports are parsed by documented rules (ending balance is not cumulative) rather than guessed. Confidentiality protects MBG's financial and employee data across the systems it touches. The standards are not separate from the accounting — they are the conditions under which the accounting can be trusted.

Resolving an ethical conflict

When facing an unresolved ethical issue, the Statement prescribes a path: first follow the organization's established policies; if unresolved, escalate up the chain of command — to the immediate supervisor, and to successively higher levels if the supervisor is involved, up to the audit committee or board. The member may contact the IMA Ethics Helpline for confidential guidance and should consider consulting their own attorney about legal rights and obligations. The member must not violate confidentiality while pursuing resolution.

CPA Crossover — REG / AUD

REG covers the regulatory and legal duties surrounding practice; AUD covers the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct, whose principles (integrity, objectivity, due care, independence) parallel the IMA standards. Expect a question naming a scenario and asking which standard it violates — conflict of interest maps to integrity, while withholding relevant information maps to credibility.

Practice and recap

  1. Name the four standards: competence, confidentiality, integrity, credibility.
  2. Map a scenario to the standard it implicates.
  3. Report exact, fully disclosed figures — credibility forbids smoothing.
  4. Resolve conflicts by following policy, escalating, using the IMA helpline, and consulting an attorney — without breaching confidentiality.

Recap: the IMA's four standards — competence, confidentiality, integrity, credibility — are the foundation under every technique in Part 2. They are why MBG's $47,200.00 gap is reported exactly and why the resolution of any conflict follows policy and the chain of command before anything else.

flashcards.front: Which standard covers conflicts of interest?
flashcards.back: Integrity — mitigate actual and avoid apparent conflicts of interest.

flashcards.front: Which standard requires disclosing all relevant information?
flashcards.back: Credibility — communicate fairly and objectively and disclose what affects users' understanding.
Maintain expertise, follow laws/standards, give accurate support, and recognize professional limitations.
Disclosing confidential information without authorization and using it for personal advantage.
Credibility forbids smoothing or summarizing away material detail.

flashcards.front: First step in resolving an ethical conflict
flashcards.back: Follow the organization's established policies for conflict resolution.

flashcards.front: Resources for an unresolved ethical conflict
flashcards.back: Escalate up the chain of command, contact the IMA Ethics Helpline, and consult your own attorney.

quiz.title: The IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four IMA standards?
questions.explain: The four standards are competence, confidentiality, integrity, and credibility — not profitability.

questions.q: An accountant with a personal financial interest approves a related payment. Which standard is implicated?
questions.explain: Mitigating conflicts of interest falls under the Integrity standard.

questions.q: Rounding away or omitting the exact $47,200.00 reconciliation gap would violate which standard?
questions.explain: Credibility requires fair, objective communication and disclosure of all relevant information.

questions.q: Using confidential MBG information for personal advantage violates:
questions.explain: Confidentiality prohibits using confidential information for personal advantage.

questions.q: Under the IMA conflict-resolution guidance, the FIRST step is to:
questions.explain: Begin by following the organization's established policies for resolving the conflict.

questions.q: Recognizing and communicating professional limitations is part of which standard?
questions.explain: Competence requires recognizing and communicating limitations that preclude responsible judgment.

questions.q: A confidential resource available to IMA members facing an ethical dilemma is the:
questions.explain: The IMA Ethics Helpline provides confidential guidance on ethical issues.
